finding: All 63 exact-target rows 11778–11840 inspected: 18 direct interests and 3 stable specializations are eligible; 26 curricular rows support construction; 9 examples and 7 outcomes remain search-only. Sixteen closest-owned generators, three responsible-technology generators and two environmental/Living generators account for all 21 eligible rows. Current programme identity, formal curriculum and specialization descriptions support the psychological, technological and social/environmental interests.
qualifications: Current Living, ICT and Robotics routes each carry 30 EC. Living is the neutral official-order choice in the current adopted regulations and cohort chart; selecting it does not erase the other stable interests. A separate environmental/built-environment UCR candidate was considered on actual course contributions and found insufficient as a complete distinct 24-course programme.

The 26 curricular rows support particular common or specialized topics; not every topic in all three specializations is compulsory in the selected Living route. The old digital-tools/wellbeing common-core assumption was replaced by current Human Factors.

Rows 11825–11833 describe possible applications such as robots and smart lighting. The underlying interests are supported, but particular current assignments were not independently confirmed. These nine rows generate no alternative.

Rows 11834–11840 are outcome/further-study leads, not employment, professional qualification or UCR-admission promises. The research-unit page is evidence of research context, not proof that every research theme is compulsory bachelor teaching.

The public specialization page mentions four technical courses; current formal 2026–27 regulations plus the cohort chart establish six named 5 EC courses/30 EC and control the reconstruction. The research course pages link current 2026 titles/codes but supply no substantive descriptions; no missing description was invented.
